sets.title: Exam 4 Practice Exam
sets.description: Exam 4 practice on ethics and law, leadership, teamwork, teaching and learning, and abbreviations and math. Exam simulation follows the professor's blueprint: 58 questions, with 17 on ethics and law, 3 abbreviations, 5 or 6 math (ice chips included), and one short case study; 29 on a phone. Practice mode follows the same blueprint, new questions first.

sets.title: Abbreviations and Math Review
sets.description: Exam 4 review, matched to the professor's Exam 4 study guide: the class's common abbreviations, unit conversions, and intake in mL, including ice chips, with the rounding and zero rules. The numbers change on every attempt.

sets.title: Sleep
sets.description: Class 20 practice: circadian rhythms and sleep hormones, the stages of sleep, what affects sleep, sleep across the lifespan, assessing sleep, sleep hygiene teaching, and the effects of poor sleep and shift work, for the Final Exam.

sets.title: Teaching and Learning
sets.description: Class 19 practice: the domains of learning, readiness to learn, planning teaching, teach-back and evaluation, teaching across the lifespan, and learning theories and the nurse's role in client education, matched to the professor's Exam 4 blueprint.

sets.title: Blood Gas Practice
sets.description: Exam 4 drill, matched to the instructor's study guide: reading arterial blood gases. Every attempt brings new numbers: say whether each value is normal, name the imbalance, and match it to its cause.

sets.title: Exam 4 Numbers to Know
sets.description: Exam 4 drill, matched to the instructor's study guide: the numbers to know, from the diabetes, cholesterol, and metabolic syndrome cutoffs to the blood gas ranges, capillary refill, the QRS, the lungs' lobes and segments, and more. Most questions show a new number on every attempt.

sets.title: The Lymphatic and Immune Systems
sets.description: Week 12, matched to the instructor's Exam 4 study guide: the lymph nodes and vessels, the bone marrow, thymus, tonsils, and spleen, the white blood cells and what each does, antibodies, memory cells, and vaccines, inflammation and its markers, and supporting immune health, with a case study.

sets.title: Exam 4 Mock Exam
sets.description: Exam 4 practice on the endocrine, cardiovascular, respiratory, and lymphatic and immune systems (Weeks 9 to 12), matched to the instructor's Exam 4 study guide and written a level beyond the real exam, with the next-generation question types. Like the real exam, each exam gives 50 questions, split evenly across the four systems, with one case study.

sets.title: Ethics Bingo
sets.description: Class 17 bingo: all 24 terms from the in-class bingo card, from advocacy to malpractice. Each term has one question that names it from its definition, and a harder one that applies it, plus a short case study.

sets.title: Leadership and Teamwork
sets.description: Class 18 practice: leaders and managers, classic and contemporary leadership styles, the functions and principles of management, interprofessional collaboration, team communication (SBAR, read-back, handoffs), and team tools for safety and conflict.

sets.title: Ethical and Legal Considerations
sets.description: Class 17 practice: values and the ethical principles, codes of ethics and client rights, ethical decision making, the sources of law and the scope of practice, federal and state laws, informed consent and advance directives, torts, negligence, and malpractice, and staffing, delegation, and reducing legal risk.

sets.title: The Respiratory System
sets.description: Week 11, matched to the instructor's Exam 4 study guide: the upper and lower airways, the alveoli and the lobes, the breathing muscles and the nervous control of breathing, ventilation, respiration, perfusion, diffusion, and mucociliary clearance, arterial blood gases, risk factors and prevention, and respiratory distress, with a case study.

sets.title: Exam 3 Challenge
sets.description: 30 harder questions for Exam 3, a level beyond the real exam: every choice sounds reasonable, most questions ask what the nurse should do first or best, and the math takes several steps, like intake with ice chips and IV pump and drip rates. Split like the real exam, 5 per area: health care systems, evidence-based practice, informatics and documentation, quality improvement, health policy, and abbreviations, med math, and orders. No case studies.

sets.title: The Cardiovascular System
sets.description: Week 10, matched to the instructor's Exam 4 study guide: blood flow through the heart, its valves, chambers, and membranes, the ECG's waves, blood components and blood type compatibility, capillary refill and arterial and venous insufficiency, thrombus, aneurysm, heart attack, murmurs, and stroke, autonomic control of the heart and blood pressure, heart-healthy habits, metabolic syndrome, and the risk factors for cardiovascular disease, with a case study.

sets.title: Abbreviations, Conversions, and Labels
sets.description: Class 10 practice for Exam 3: common medical abbreviations, including spotting the wrong one in a documentation entry, complete medication orders, units of measure, metric, household, weight, length, time, and temperature conversions, dose calculations, intake in mL, and reading medication labels.

sets.title: The Endocrine System
sets.description: Week 9, matched to the instructor's Exam 4 study guide: the hormones of the hypothalamus, pituitary, thyroid, parathyroid, adrenal glands, pancreas, pineal gland, and gonads, the TSH test, cortisol and how it's measured, diabetes mellitus (diagnosis, risk factors, and signs), metabolic syndrome, and the signs and symptoms of endocrine problems, with a case study.

sets.title: Healthcare Systems
sets.description: Class 11 practice: levels of prevention and care, care delivery and payment models, access to care and social determinants of health, and allocation of resources.

sets.title: Evidence-Based Practice
sets.description: Class 12 practice: how EBP evolved, its links to other concepts and how it differs from the nursing process, barriers and resistance to change, research basics, the steps of EBP and PICOT questions, and individual and organizational EBP, including following facility policy and procedure.

sets.title: Informatics and Documentation
sets.description: Class 13 practice: informatics in nursing, health information technology, decision support and health literacy, confidentiality and protecting client information (HIPAA), documentation guidelines and formats such as PIE and DAR, and the legal side of documentation.

sets.title: Quality Improvement
sets.description: Class 14 practice: why quality must improve, federal, state, and local initiatives, nurse-sensitive indicators, the QI process, chart audits, and risk management, incident reports, and quality management programs such as PDSA and root cause analysis.

sets.title: Health Policy
sets.description: Class 15 practice: health policy as an entity and a process, how policy is made, key health laws such as HIPAA and the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act, agencies such as the FDA and professional associations, accreditation, and insurance and reimbursement.

sets.title: Exam 3 Practice Exam
sets.description: All three Exam 3 topics in one practice exam: the integumentary system, the nervous system, and the senses. Each exam gives 25 of the 150 questions, spread evenly across the three topics.

sets.title: The Senses
sets.description: Week 8, matched to the Exam 3 study guide: touch, proprioception, and interoception, the eye and how vision works, eye tests (Snellen, Ishihara, Amsler grid, and tonometry) and eye findings, the ear and hearing, balance, and taste and smell.

sets.title: The Integumentary System
sets.description: Week 6, matched to the Exam 3 study guide: skin cells and mechanoreceptors, the skin assessment, signs of skin dysfunction and edema, common skin findings, mole checks and IV skin prep, skin medications, and other findings.

sets.title: Exam 3 Mock Exam
sets.description: A practice exam that follows the Exam 3 blueprint and the professor's review, written a little harder than the real exam. Each exam gives 60 questions, split the way the real exam is, from a pool of about 130: 10 each on health care systems, evidence-based practice, informatics and documentation (3 on confidentiality), quality improvement (2 on the PDSA cycle), and health policy (2 on the Mental Health Parity Act and 4 on HIPAA, PHI, the FDA, and health literacy), plus 3 abbreviations, 6 med math (3 fill in the blank), and 1 prescriber's order. The math questions get new numbers on every attempt. Like the real exam, it has no case studies.

sets.title: The Nervous System
sets.description: Week 7, matched to the Exam 3 study guide: how the nervous system is organized, neurons and glial cells, nerve impulses and synapses, the brain, spinal cord, and meninges, cranial nerves, the autonomic nervous system, the Glasgow Coma Scale, and meningitis, intracranial pressure, and seizures.

sets.title: Med-Surg Sample Set
sets.description: A sample med-surg exam with every question type, including a 4-question COPD case study.
